findings.text: HF-2 spent about 91 seconds between creation and start, because it was assigned only after HF-1 had cleared its build and review. Its own build took about 36 seconds.
HF-1's build time covers two Builder runs because of the send-back. The first run completed the file without the requested second line, and the rework run added it.
No time was spent in the check gate. Every completion recorded that no check ran because the project configures no fast check.

findings.text: The build names a Builder and a Checker, but the per-task builder and checker fields are all null, and no check run was recorded. The build ran with no checker involvement.
The two tasks ran one after the other on a single Builder. HF-2 was not assigned until HF-1 had left the build and review loop.
The rework run after the send-back cost about as much as the original run on the same task. Both runs are recorded separately, so the extra cost of the send-back is visible per run.
The Builder's tool list did not include submit_checkpoint_notes. The run used update_task notes instead and also wrote a file under .agentweave/calls as a workaround.
Both accepted decisions carry the reason `the drive's operator`, which says nothing about why the evidence was accepted.
HF-1's task notes still say the evidence is `awaiting decision`, but the evidence was first held and later accepted, so the notes are out of date.
Completions logged that no check ran, so the completion step gives no automated verification in this project.

what_worked.text: The send-back loop moved from revision_needed to in_progress almost immediately, and the rework run finished in about 42 seconds.
The Builder stayed in scope. HF-1 changed only hello.txt, and the first run did not pick up HF-2 because the loop briefing said not to.
HF-2 was built in one run with no send-back, and its evidence was accepted on the first review.

improvements.label: code_and_checks
improvements.text: Configure a fast check for this project so that task completions run an automated verification and no longer log that no check ran.

improvements.label: staffing_and_running
improvements.text: Name the Builder and Checker per task when a build is staffed at the reviewed level, and run the checker so the build has a check run.

improvements.label: tooling
improvements.text: Make submit_checkpoint_notes available to Builder runs, or document update_task notes as the fallback, so that Builders do not write workaround files under .agentweave/calls.

improvements.label: tooling
improvements.text: Record a meaningful reason on accepted evidence decisions instead of the placeholder `the drive's operator`, and refresh task notes when evidence changes state.

lessons.text: When the project has no fast check configured, completions run no automated verification. Builders should run and record their own verification in the evidence.
Builders here work one task at a time, so a second task waits until the first has cleared review. Plan timing with that queue in mind.
The checkpoint-notes tool may be absent from a Builder's tool list. If it is, record checkpoint notes in update_task notes and say so in the final message.
